title: Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus
source: Three ordinary foundation photographs and the pinned standard PMTiles/Mapzen museum context; approximate visualization registration.
axis: +X east-northeast along the inferred museum-parallel wall; +Y up; +Z south-southeast toward the photographed exposed face. Approximate signed visualization frame, uncertainty45degrees.

nativeAxes.x: east-northeast along the inferred long wall

identityStatus: Q586468 identifies the surviving temple foundations. Photographs place the exposed tufa wall inside the Esedra/Capitoline museum complex. The PMTiles museum polygon and approximate photographic camera location constrain an explicitly estimated frame; they do not supply an ancient wall footprint.

orientationControl.basis: Approximate current buried-foundation placement inside the mapped Esedra, not a reconstruction of the lost temple. The long wall follows the museum envelope axis; its exposed face points south-southeast toward the approximate2024 photographic camera location. Exact ancient wall coordinates and excavation levels are not mapped. The entire model envelope fits inside the retained museum part. The minimum native DEM vertex covering that envelope supplies a conservative overburden reference: modelY8.982m attaches there, leaving the highest modeled stone at least0.3m below the unchanged terrain. This preserves the modern surface and museum; it is an approximate burial envelope, not a measured excavation floor. SourceY0 is the displayed foundation base. No terrain/building/water removal. The normal above-ground world should not expose this basement wall; below-grade or isolated inspection is needed. Exact museum interior, excavation shape and buried masonry beyond the photographed visible remnants are not modeled.

geometryRole: Independent modern museum context, transformed into the declared photographic model frame; not an ancient temple footprint.

reconstruction.scope: Unfinished photographic draft of the exposed tufa foundation wall and adjoining low remnants of the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus. It does not represent the complete buried temple footprint. No lost ancient roof, columns, cellae or statues are reconstructed, and no modern museum architecture is replaced.
